signal: Sage raised a $65M Series C led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives and launched Tasking, an EHR-integrated senior-care workflow

email.body1:
Shane, saw Sage raised a $65M Series C and launched Tasking, the EHR-integrated workflow for senior care.

Scaling that fast usually means more in-market accounts than the team can cover before new reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount, 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Sage off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing those progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Shane, quick follow-up for Sage.

Post-raise, board expectations on pipeline jump faster than headcount can. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the new number, so the gap surfaces late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Sage needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Shane, last bit of proof for Sage.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Sage's reply rate likely compares to other Series-C health-tech startups. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Shane, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem. The fundraise-to-hiring stretch is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a Series-C health-tech motion? I'll tailor it to Sage either way.
